prompt.context_jp: 舞台___、オリンピック景気に沸く東京の一角にある小さな不動産営業所だ。
prompt.prompt_jp: 舞台___、オリンピック景気に沸く東京の一角にある小さな不動産営業所だ。
prompt.prompt_en: Narrator sets the scene. Which particle marks 舞台 as the topic being defined?

feedback.correct_en: The narrator is announcing the topic ('As for the setting, it is...') — classic は for defining/introducing a known topic.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would mark 舞台 as newly identified information in a presentational sense, but here 舞台 is the frame being described, not newly spotted.

prompt.context_jp: そこに現れた一人の女___、穏やかだった日々を少しずつ塗り替えつつあった。
prompt.prompt_jp: そこに現れた一人の女___、穏やかだった日々を少しずつ塗り替えつつあった。
prompt.prompt_en: A new character is being introduced to the story. Which particle fits?

feedback.correct_en: が introduces this woman as new information — she just appeared and the sentence identifies her as the agent of change.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would treat her as an already-known topic, but the sentence is presenting her for the first time.

prompt.context_jp: 「私___売れない家はありません！」
prompt.prompt_jp: 「私___売れない家はありません！」
prompt.prompt_en: Machi's catchphrase. Which particle marks '私' as the one for whom no house is unsellable?

feedback.correct_en: に marks the experiencer/dative — 'for me / to me, there is no house I can't sell.' It's the standard pattern 〜に〜がある.
feedback.incorrect_en: で would mark means/location, and を would mark a direct object — neither fits an existential 'ある' with an experiencer.

contrast_examples.jp: 私にできないことはない。

contrast_examples.en: I can solve it (using myself as the means).

prompt.context_jp: 「私に売れない家___ありません！」
prompt.prompt_jp: 「私に売れない家___ありません！」
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle fits in Machi's declaration?

feedback.correct_en: は here signals a sweeping topic/negative claim: 'as for unsellable houses, there are none.' Negative existence sweeps naturally use は.
feedback.incorrect_en: 家がありません would just mean 'there is no house' and loses the categorical boast Machi is making.

prompt.context_jp: 「それって 三軒家チーフ___来たからじゃ？」
prompt.prompt_jp: 「それって 三軒家チーフ___来たからじゃ？」
prompt.prompt_en: Explaining why sales improved. Which particle names the cause-agent?

feedback.correct_en: Inside the 〜から clause the subject is new/identifying ('because Chief Sangenya came'), so が is natural.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would float the chief up as the main topic of the whole sentence, but the speaker is just citing her arrival as the reason.

prompt.context_jp: 「ミーティング中の私語___禁止」
prompt.prompt_jp: 「ミーティング中の私語___禁止」
prompt.prompt_en: Machi lays down a rule. Which particle fits?

feedback.correct_en: は marks 私語 as the topic of a general rule: 'As for private chatter, it's forbidden.' Rules/definitions typically take は.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would sound like a reactive report ('chatter is [happening and] forbidden'), not a standing rule.

prompt.context_jp: 三軒家___、表情ひとつ変えずにまっすぐ正面を見つめていた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 三軒家___、表情ひとつ変えずにまっすぐ正面を見つめていた。
prompt.prompt_en: Others react in various ways, but Sangenya alone is stoic. Which particle marks the contrast?

feedback.correct_en: だけは highlights Sangenya in contrast to everyone else described in the previous sentences — classic contrastive は.
feedback.incorrect_en: だけが would simply identify her as the exclusive subject but loses the comparative nuance against the others' reactions.

contrast_examples.jp: 彼女だけは笑わなかった。
彼女だけが知っている。

prompt.context_jp: 屋代___が、我が子を自慢する父親のような顔で満足げにうなずいていた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 屋代___が、我が子を自慢する父親のような顔で満足げにうなずいていた。
prompt.prompt_en: Only Yashiro was nodding proudly. Which particle fits the 'only X' meaning?

feedback.correct_en: だけが = exhaustive listing: 'Yashiro, and only Yashiro, was nodding proudly.' The following が identifies him as the sole subject.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would make Yashiro a general topic and lose the 'only he' exclusivity that the scene requires.

prompt.context_jp: 「家を売るの___個人技です」
prompt.prompt_jp: 「家を売るの___個人技です」
prompt.prompt_en: Machi defines selling houses as a solo skill. Which particle fits?

feedback.correct_en: This is a definition/thesis: 'As for selling houses, it's an individual skill.' Definitions take は.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would make it a reactive identification ('it is selling houses that is an individual skill') which doesn't fit her blunt assertion.

prompt.context_jp: 「売るなら 全部 私___売ります」
prompt.prompt_jp: 「売るなら 全部 私___売ります」
prompt.prompt_en: Machi insists she will sell them all herself. Which particle fits?

feedback.correct_en: Exhaustive-listing が: 'It is I (and no one else) who will sell them.' が emphasizes the exclusive agent.
feedback.incorrect_en: 私は売ります would just be a topic statement ('as for me, I'll sell'), losing the 'only me' punch Machi wants.

prompt.context_jp: サンルームのある一戸建ての前___は朝から庭野が立ち、通りがかる人々に何度も頭を下げていた。
prompt.prompt_jp: サンルームのある一戸建ての前___朝から庭野が立ち、通りがかる人々に頭を下げていた。
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle marks the location where Niwano was standing all morning (action location)?

feedback.correct_en: 立つ with a stative, posture-holding sense takes に (location of existence/placement). '前に立つ' = stand positioned in front.
feedback.incorrect_en: で marks the location of a dynamic action, but here 立つ expresses being stationed/positioned, so に is natural.

contrast_examples.en: He is standing in front of the gate (position).
He talked in front of the gate (action venue).

prompt.context_jp: 「家 買う気もないのに 足立のこと___んだよ」
prompt.prompt_jp: 「家 買う気もないのに 足立のこと___んだよ」
prompt.prompt_en: Yashiro explains the 'Adachi Club' madams. Choose the verb.

feedback.correct_en: 追っかける = to chase/follow (as a fan). The 'Adachi Club' are groupies who chase him, matching the gag.
feedback.incorrect_en: 見送る means to see someone off; 見逃す means to overlook. Neither captures the fan-chasing behavior.

contrast_examples.jp: アイドルを追っかける。
contrast_examples.en: To chase after an idol (fan behavior).

prompt.context_jp: 「日差し___ ず～っと強くて」
prompt.prompt_jp: 「日差し___ ず～っと強くて」
prompt.prompt_en: The customer wants permanent sunshine, contrasting with the sunshade feature. Which particle?

feedback.correct_en: Contrastive は: she's responding to the offer to block the sun — 'as for sunlight (I want it) strong all the time.' The は contrasts with the implied 'other things'.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would be a neutral description of a current state, not a preference contrasted with Adachi's proposal.

contrast_examples.jp: 日差しは強いほうがいい。
contrast_examples.en: I prefer sunlight strong (contrast with alternative).

prompt.context_jp: 「父___死んだ時に相続したお金で買ったんですけど」
prompt.prompt_jp: 「父___死んだ時に相続したお金で買ったんですけど」
prompt.prompt_en: Inside the subordinate 時 clause, which particle marks 父?

feedback.correct_en: Subordinate clauses (〜時, 〜から, 〜のに) typically mark their internal subject with が, not は. '父が死んだ時' = when my father died.
feedback.incorrect_en: 父は死んだ時 breaks the subordinate-clause pattern; は tends to float up to the main clause.

contrast_examples.jp: 雨が降る時は家にいる。
contrast_examples.en: When it rains, I stay home.

prompt.context_jp: 「このお部屋___私が必ず売ります」
prompt.prompt_jp: 「このお部屋___私が必ず売ります」
prompt.prompt_en: Machi promises Natsuki. Which particle fits the object/topic 'this room'?

feedback.correct_en: このお部屋は fronts the object as topic: 'As for this room, I will definitely sell it.' This also sets up 私が as exhaustive-listing — 'I (and only I) will sell it.'
feedback.incorrect_en: が on お部屋 would make the room the subject, conflicting with 売ります, which needs 私 as subject.

contrast_examples.jp: この家は私が売ります。

prompt.context_jp: 「できるヤツっていうのは 周りを___しまうんだな」
prompt.prompt_jp: 「できるヤツっていうのは 周りを___しまうんだな
prompt.prompt_en: Fuse's cynical take. Choose the verb.

feedback.correct_en: 不幸にする = make unhappy. Fuse is grumbling that competent people make everyone around them miserable.
feedback.incorrect_en: 幸せにする (make happy) would reverse his cynical point; 便利にする doesn't apply to people.

contrast_examples.en: A person who makes those around miserable.

prompt.context_jp: 「サンチーが来て 売り上げ上がったもんだから⇒ ___が出ちまったんだなぁ」
prompt.prompt_jp: 「売り上げ上がったもんだから ___が出ちまったんだなぁ」
prompt.prompt_en: Fuse says the manager got greedy. Which noun fits '〜が出る'?

feedback.correct_en: 欲が出る = to become greedy / to start wanting more. Standard idiom for ambition surfacing.
feedback.incorrect_en: 涙が出る (tears welling up) and 元気が出る (gaining energy) don't match Fuse's complaint about the manager getting ambitious.

contrast_examples.jp: つい欲が出てしまった。

prompt.context_jp: 三軒家の言葉___本当なのか、それとも単なるはったりなのか、誰にも判断がつかなかった。
prompt.prompt_jp: 三軒家の言葉___本当なのか、それとも単なるはったりなのか、誰にも判断がつかなかった。
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle fits inside the embedded 'whether ~' question?

feedback.correct_en: Embedded のか/かどうか questions typically take が for the subject — this is a subordinate clause, not a main-clause topic.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would promote 言葉 to the main topic, but here it's the subject inside the embedded question about truth vs. bluff.

contrast_examples.jp: 彼が来るかどうか分からない。
contrast_examples.en: I don't know whether he's coming.

prompt.context_jp: その静けさを破ったの___、机の上の電話だった。
prompt.prompt_jp: その静けさを破ったの___、机の上の電話だった。
prompt.prompt_en: Narration identifies what broke the silence. Which particle?

feedback.correct_en: The cleft 〜のは…だ pattern uses は on the のは part: 'The thing that broke the silence was the phone.' This frames the predicate as the identifying answer.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would turn it into 'the one that broke the silence' as new information, but the cleft structure here specifically uses は.

prompt.context_jp: 「ＳＮＳで___させました」
prompt.prompt_jp: 「ＳＮＳで___させました」
prompt.prompt_en: Machi explains her marketing trick. Choose the verb.

feedback.correct_en: 拡散する = to spread/go viral (on social media). It's the standard verb for info spreading online.
feedback.incorrect_en: 分散 means to disperse/distribute (e.g. risks); 発散 means to vent/release (e.g. stress). Neither fits viral marketing.

prompt.context_jp: 腕が確かなのは間違いない___、その正体はいまだに見えないのだ。
prompt.prompt_jp: 腕が確かなのは間違いない___、その正体はいまだに見えないのだ。
prompt.prompt_en: Which conjunction fits? ('her skill is sure, BUT her identity is unclear')

feedback.correct_en: Sentence-connective が means 'but/however' — it fits the contrast between confirmed skill and unknown identity.
feedback.incorrect_en: ので and から express cause, which contradicts the contrastive relationship between the two clauses.

contrast_examples.en: I'm tired, but I'll push on.

prompt.context_jp: 庭野「もうお引っ越しの準備をされたのですか？」保坂の返事として自然なのは？
prompt.prompt_en: Which reply is more natural in context for the minimalist Hosaka?

choices.text: いえ 普段から こんな感じです。これで いいのです。
いえ いつもだから こんな感じ。これで いいんだ。

feedback.correct_en: Hosaka speaks politely to the realtors he's just met; です-form keeps the register appropriate for a first-time client visit.
feedback.incorrect_en: The plain-form version is too casual for addressing agents he just invited into his home.

contrast_examples.en: This is just how I like it (polite declarative).
This is fine (casual, to self or close friends).

prompt.context_jp: 「生きるということは ___いくことです」
prompt.prompt_jp: 「生きるということは ___いくことです」
prompt.prompt_en: Hosaka's minimalist philosophy. Which verb fits '〜ていく'?

feedback.correct_en: そぎ落とす = to shave off / strip away. It matches Hosaka's minimalist worldview of cutting away the unnecessary.
feedback.incorrect_en: 積み上げる (pile up) is the opposite of minimalism; 投げ出す (abandon) is too negative and doesn't fit his tidy philosophy.

prompt.context_jp: 「よろしければ ___ お話を伺いたく存じますが」
prompt.prompt_jp: 「よろしければ ___ お話を伺いたく存じますが」
prompt.prompt_en: Machi's humble business phrase. Fill in the honorific verb.

feedback.correct_en: お目にかかる is humble (謙譲語) for '会う' — the speaker humbles herself when offering to meet the customer.
feedback.incorrect_en: お会いになる is honorific (尊敬語) — it would elevate oneself, which is backwards. 見て is far too casual and wrong meaning.

contrast_examples.jp: お目にかかれて光栄です。

contrast_examples.en: The president will meet [you] (honorific toward president).

prompt.context_jp: 「ローン___ 即金でお買い上げでしたら 1億まで お下げできます」
prompt.prompt_jp: 「ローン___ 即金でお買い上げでしたら 1億まで お下げできます」
prompt.prompt_en: Adachi's negotiation line. Fill in.

feedback.correct_en: ではなく = 'not X but Y'. 'If (payment is) not a loan but cash...' — Adachi is contrasting the two payment methods.
feedback.incorrect_en: のように (like) and だから (because) break the X-not-Y-but comparison the sentence requires.

contrast_examples.jp: 現金ではなくカードで。

prompt.context_jp: 狭小住宅を売ると宣言する三軒家のセリフ。彼女のキャラに最も合うのは？
prompt.prompt_en: Which line best fits Machi's blunt, exhaustive-listing style?

choices.text: 私は売れると思います。
私も売ってみたいです。

feedback.correct_en: 私が売ります uses exhaustive-listing が — 'I (and no one else) will sell it.' This matches Machi's blunt, self-assertive style throughout the episode.
feedback.incorrect_en: は softens to 'as for me, I think I can'; も (also/too) collaborates with others — both lose Machi's exclusive, confident claim.

contrast_examples.en: I will sell it (and only me).

prompt.context_jp: 客から「図面だけではダメですよね？」と聞かれた三軒家の返事として自然なのは？
prompt.prompt_en: Which reply by Machi to the client sounds more natural and polite?

choices.text: はい 拝見しないと ご仲介はできかねます。
はい 見ないと 仲介できないです。

feedback.correct_en: 拝見する (humble for 見る) and できかねます (polite negative potential) fit the formal client-facing context — the registered style Machi actually uses.
feedback.incorrect_en: The plain 見ない / できない is too flat for a first client meeting at a real-estate agency.

contrast_examples.jp: ご仲介はできかねます。
